dosing.evidence: intraperitoneal (ip) injection of either psilocybin (2 mg/kg in 0.1 mL saline)

handling.evidence: Paper does not mention handling procedures.

assays.assay_name: Video Arena - Cage Exploration and Head-Twitch Response
assays.assay_description: Custom video tracking arena: black acrylic box with smaller clear acrylic inner box containing bedding, lid covered, recorded from above at 150 fps for 40-60 min post-injection. Frame-difference analysis quantified gross movement (cage exploration); head-twitch responses were manually scored from the same videos.

application_type.evidence: intraperitoneal (ip) injection of either psilocybin (2 mg/kg in 0.1 mL saline)

setup_habituation.evidence: Behavioral experiments began with habituation, by placing the mouse in the small clear box for an hour, before being administered an intraperitoneal (ip) injection

setup_restrain.evidence: the mouse was placed back in the clear box, covered with a clear lid, and then videoed

food_restriction.evidence: No food mentioned in apparatus; standard short-term behavioral arena.

water_restriction.evidence: No water mentioned in apparatus; standard short-term behavioral arena.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after injection, the mouse was placed back in the clear box ... and then videoed for an additional 40-60 min.

sample_size.evidence: psilocybin (2 mg/kg in 0.1 mL saline) (n = 5 mice) or a 0.1 mL saline vehicle (n = 5 mice). HTR manually scored in n=1 psilocybin and n=1 saline mouse.

outcomes.summary: A 2 mg/kg ip dose of psilocybin increased head-twitch rate transiently (peaking within the first 10 min and declining by ~10 min post-injection) and produced a biphasic locomotor response: mice explored the arena during the first 10 min but became significantly hypoactive for the remaining 10-60 min relative to both their early exploration and saline controls. Saline mice showed consistent movement throughout.
outcomes.statistics: Psilocybin 0-10 vs 10-60: bootstrap t test P = 0.012; Saline 10-60 vs Psilocybin 10-60: bootstrap t test P = 0.011; Saline 0-10 vs 10-60: P = 0.66; HTR/CE correlation saline vs psilocybin: bootstrap t test P = 0.026.
outcomes.evidence: the psilocybin 10-60 movement was significantly less than both the psilocybin 0-10 movement (bootstrap t test, P = 0.012) and the saline 10-60 movement (bootstrap t test, P = 0.011).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Cage exploration movement trace plus manually-labeled head-twitch responses; HTR/CE correlation also computed.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: time-course of cage exploration plotted on a frame-by-frame basis; averaged in 0-10 vs 10-60 min windows; HTR time-course also analyzed.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions, sequences, or microstructure.

B4_ethological.evidence: Measures are HTR (excluded per rubric) and gross locomotor movement (not ethological).

B5_social.evidence: Mouse tested alone in the clear box.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Movement quantified via frame-difference and Hilbert envelope; HTRs were manually labeled. No pose estimation or ML classifier.

E1_environment_type.evidence: custom-built video tracking arena ... large black acrylic box ... contained a smaller clear acrylic box

E2_shelter.evidence: Clear box covered with a clear lid; no enclosed refuge.

E3_bedding.evidence: Bedding was placed inside the clear box

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material mentioned in the testing arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects mentioned in the arena.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single clear acrylic box used for testing.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mouse tested alone in the box.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water present in the testing arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: videoed for an additional 40-60 min after injection

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single recording session per mouse on injection day.

D4_baseline.evidence: Habituation occurred before injection but no pre-drug behavioral data was recorded/reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Recording was acute (0-60 min post-injection); no >=24 h follow-up.

judge_notes: Merged GLM's separate 'Open Field Test' and 'Head-Twitch Response' assays into one entry: both measures were collected from the same video recording in the same custom arena during a single session, with HTR being one manually-scored measure and cage exploration being the automated frame-difference measure. Qwen and gptoss correctly treated this as one assay.

Did NOT score two-photon imaging or wide-field tonotopic imaging as behavioral assays - these are neural recording sessions in head-fixed awake mice with passive sound presentation; per rubric they are excluded.
B1 scored 2-3 because two distinct behavioural measures (gross movement/CE and HTR count) plus a derived correlation were reported.
Sex coded as 'both' based on imaging cohort breakdown (2F/4M psilocybin, 3M saline); behavioral cohort sex not separately specified.
